Native relay setup and builds

Install, activate and build the native connected-machine relay without replacing its registration.

About 13 min read · 2 sections

On this page
01 Activation 02 Build and checks

Return to the native connected-machine overview.

Activation

The old transport and the relay cannot own the same machine concurrently. Quit ChatGPT normally on the test machine before activation. The installer never quits the app. Install a release containing the relay, then run:

gateway native install
gateway desktop register
gateway desktop
gateway native status

The per-user LaunchAgent starts at login and restarts after a crash. SDK heartbeats, acknowledgements, chunks, and reconnects carry the remote app-server messages. The local adapter obtains real remote-control status and methods through an owned private Unix socket. Its original executor's remote transport is disabled only for that process. The primary configuration stays unchanged.

Existing registrations are bound to their native account. Signing out or changing that account stops the relay's existing connection. It cannot silently adopt a different account or create a new connected computer.

Registering a relay under the unified service

A consolidated Mac whose relay slot waits as not_registered registers the relay the service already runs, with ChatGPT quit normally:

gateway native install

Under a unified plan this installs no LaunchAgent. It takes the relay binary, relay home, native home and app CLI from the plan's native component, refuses while ChatGPT is open, and runs the relay's --check against this account's existing, enabled Codex Desktop registration. A missing or disabled registration is refused, and the relay never enrolls a new machine. Running it again with the same plan changes nothing.

A registered relay owns remote control. OpenAI allows one remote-control connection per Mac, so an engine that connects first leaves the relay with HTTP error: 409 Conflict on every retry until that engine exits. Once the relay is registered, every adapter, SSH listener and shared host starts its stock engine with remote control switched off, whether or not the relay is connected at that moment. The environment switch applies only to engine startup; it does not make a later remoteControl/enable safe. Therefore a registered relay owns every remoteControl/* request, even when its cloud status is errored or its private socket is temporarily absent. The adapter reconnects that socket automatically. While it is unavailable, those control requests fail with the relay error; they never fall back to the stock engine. A registered relay that is down for a while means the phone loses this Mac until the relay is back; no other engine takes its place. A 409 Conflict in the relay log can indicate a competing engine, including an older adapter that allowed an enable request while the relay was unavailable; it is not proof of the exact holder.

The install avoids that race in this order:

  1. It writes <state>/native-registration.pending. Adapters and listeners that start from now on already count the relay as registered. The previous native-registration.json is not touched, so it is the rollback. A pending record older than ten minutes (a dead install) counts as none.
  2. It looks for stock engines under this gateway's adapters, SSH listeners and shared host that started before the pending record (it reads the process list in the C locale and refuses if any line cannot be read). A first registration only; a Mac that already registered a relay has none to clear.
    • An SSH listener is never killed from outside. The install sends it SIGUSR2, a request to retire. The listener decides itself, in one step, whether it is truly idle: no request in flight, no turn running, no approval waiting, and 30 seconds without traffic. If so it stops the way a TERM would and the remote app reconnects through a fresh listener, which stands down. Otherwise it ignores the request and says so in its record, and the install refuses with "an SSH session from another Mac is using this Mac; retry when it is idle".
    • The signal is sent only to a listener whose record (listener-activity-<pid>.json beside its socket) names the same start time as the process list. A listener from a release before 0.4.8 keeps no record and would die of that signal, so the install refuses with "a listener from an older release is running; quit ChatGPT on the other Mac, wait about 2 minutes, then retry".
    • Another Codex session on this Mac that runs its own engine also refuses the install. The shared host's engine is not signalled: the service restarts the host, once idle, because the pending record already counts as a registration; the install waits for it and refuses if the host stays busy. The steps run in this order so that a refusal changes as little as possible: the checks that need no action come first, then the shared host (waited for up to about 30 seconds, while the service restarts it when idle), and only then are the listeners asked, one by one. Any refusal removes the pending record and registers nothing. If a listener declines after an earlier one already retired, the earlier one stays retired; that is harmless, because its remote app reconnects through a fresh listener that stands down.
  3. It runs the relay's --enable and waits up to 45 seconds. On success it writes <state>/native-registration.json and removes the pending record. On a timeout or an early exit it keeps the previous registration exactly as it was, removes the pending record and reports the fixed reason.

The service notices the registration within about two seconds (not at the five-minute check) and starts the relay while ChatGPT stays closed, so the slot is not left free. Each SSH listener keeps listener-activity-<pid>.json beside its socket (pid, start time, whether any turn or approval is in flight, when it last declined a retire request); it is removed when the listener exits. A shared host that started before the registration restarts when idle so its engine stands down too. Nothing hands remote control back to an engine while the relay is registered, so a relay that stays broken leaves the phone without this Mac.

Giving remote control back. gateway native uninstall under the unified service now writes {"registered":false} to <state>/native-registration.json, keeps the previous record as native-registration.json.pre-relay-off-<time> and removes a pending record. Only engines that start afterwards keep their own remote control; running ones keep standing down until they restart, and a service restart does not make the desktop app or SSH listeners release it:

  • the desktop app: quit ChatGPT, and open it again once the rest has let go;
  • SSH listeners: they let go the next time they start, that is when the remote app next connects after its listener exits;
  • the relay and the shared host: restart the service while idle (gateway service restart).

gateway health warns when a registered relay has been paused for more than five minutes, or runs but has not been connected for that long. The "not connected" time is measured from the last moment the service saw the relay connected (lastConnectedAt in its status file), or from the relay's start if it never was, because the relay rewrites its own status file on every change and a refused connection (HTTP 409) changes it constantly. The warning names the cause class (the relay keeps failing, or the service has not started it since the registration) and this command.

Moving a Mac to the 0.163 relay

Before this release the relay refused the 0.163 engine, so the phone used ChatGPT's own remote control, which lists only openai chats and would send gateway model aliases to OpenAI. What to expect depends on the Mac:

Mac Plan Relay slot before After this release
Studio, macbook-server sharedNativeExecutor: false (set on 17 October) paused: failing where a relay is registered, not_registered on macbook-server Relay sessions retain private native engines until native sharing is explicitly adopted
A Mac with sharedNativeExecutor: true Host shares native chats paused, failing The verified 0.163 host shares native work; clients detach without stopping its SDK

A relay that the service starts again does not restart the host (resumePaused in src/service-supervisor.ts), and the host and each adapter decide once, at start, whether the registered relay owns remote control (the registration, not the relay's live status, decides; see Registering a relay under the unified service). So the order is: the relay connects first, then the service restarts while idle, then ChatGPT opens. An engine that started before the relay was registered keeps its remote control until it exits; a 409 Conflict in the relay log means exactly that, and gateway native install retires idle SSH listeners for that reason. Except for quitting and reopening ChatGPT, which the user does normally, the steps below only read state or use the gateway's own commands.

  1. Before the install, check the app engine and the current state:

    /Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/bin/codex --version
codesign -dv --verbose=2 /Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/CodexCLI.app/Contents/MacOS/codex 2>&1 | grep TeamIdentifier
gateway service status
gateway native status

    Expect codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.10.2, TeamIdentifier=2DC432GLL2, the native component paused with its reason, and executionHost.sharedNativeExecutor (false on Studio and macbook-server).

  2. Install the release as usual. The installer never quits the app.

  3. When no chat is running, quit ChatGPT normally with Command-Q.

  4. Only where the slot was not_registered (macbook-server): run gateway native install. It retires idle SSH listeners and refuses while one is busy. A slot paused as failing needs nothing; the new relay binary is the change the five-minute check waits for.

  5. Wait a few seconds (up to five minutes if the install was not the trigger) with ChatGPT still closed, then check gateway native status: relay.status connected with the original environmentId, and gateway service status: the native component running with no pausedReason.

  6. Still with ChatGPT closed and no chat running, restart the service so the host and the adapters start beside the live relay:

    gateway service restart
gateway versions --check
gateway service status
gateway health --json
grep -h -E '"event":"(component_resumed|component_paused|native_sharing_unavailable|native_sharing_fallback)"' STATE/telemetry/events-$(date +%F).jsonl

    Expect every process on the new release, executionHost.state running, the relay still connected, and one component_resumed. On a Mac whose plan shares native chats, native_sharing_unavailable with reason: sdk_version is expected. STATE is the gateway state directory.

  7. Open ChatGPT normally. Its adapter finds the live relay, so the app's engine runs with its own remote control turned off and remoteControl/* reaches the relay.

  8. On the phone, open this Mac's Codex chats. The list comes from the gateway router; gateway chats saved under the legacy provider appear when the router adds that provider to an unfiltered list. Continue one gateway chat and one native chat. A native chat that is open in the Mac's app is refused with already has an active writer until the app lets it go.

  9. In the relay log, expect session_started and session_ended records, an rc_connected SDK label, and no session_rejected.

Native sharing can be staged on the verified release with gateway service shared-native --on-restart, preserving the active service plan until a safe primary daemon start. Include --with-gateway explicitly on an installation that also needs gateway sharing. See travel recovery. Old adapters and uncertain writers defer adoption instead of being stopped.

If the relay stays paused, gateway service status names the reason. failing after the install means the relay still refuses the engine or cannot start; the relay log names the cause, and ChatGPT keeps its own remote control meanwhile. To go back, install the previous release: its relay refuses 0.163 and is set aside again, and the registration written by gateway native install stays, so the newer release picks the relay up again.

gateway native uninstall stops this managed transport and keeps its private state. A fresh normal app launch restores the original remote transport. Explicit uninstall cancels remote work. A changed running registration is refused until the old service is stopped after active chats finish.

Build and checks

The relay links the Apache-2.0 Codex SDK from the exact upstream commit documented in native-relay/NOTICE. The build downloads a checksum-pinned archive into gateway-owned build storage. On every build it rewrites the patched files from pristine archive bytes: the outgoing-envelope, server-name and existing-enrollment guards, and the small hooks for the behaviour above. Each patch anchor must occur an exact number of times. The hook logic lives in native-relay/sdk-overlay, which may only add files. The signed desktop bundle is unchanged. The installer carries the SDK license, notice, and dependency inventory.

node scripts/build-native-relay.mjs --test --dev
node scripts/build-native-relay.mjs
node scripts/build-release.mjs --with-native

The sources, pristine copies and crate manifest are kept per pinned revision (sdk-<revision>, build-<revision> and sdk-<revision>.tar.gz in .state/native-relay-build). The gateway SDK build reads its own pinned archive from sdk.tar.gz in the same folder, so building the relay never replaces it. The relay repairs its own lockfile with scripts/native-relay-sdk-lock.mjs: the 0.163 archive keeps 0.0.0 for 160 source-less workspace packages, and only those are set to 0.163.0-alpha.10.2.

The end-to-end check runs the built relay against the real signed app engine and mock upstreams only:

node scripts/e2e-native-relay.mjs --root /tmp/gwrl-$(date +%s)

A localhost mock plays the ChatGPT backend and the phone. It hands out the server token, accepts the relay's websocket and sends remote-control envelopes. The state is a Mac like Studio or macbook-server: a unified plan with sharedNativeExecutor: false and a registered relay. The relay starts each stream's gateway codex-shim session, and the router runs the real engine privately for a native chat and a gateway executor for a gateway chat, both answering from the mock. The run checks that the relay:

  • accepts the 0.163 and 0.162 CLIs and refuses others;
  • refreshes the server token for the original registration and never enrolls;
  • connects with the original server ID, name and installation ID;
  • answers remoteControl/status/read itself and passes model/list and thread/list to the router;
  • runs both chats, and continues the gateway chat with its history on a second stream;
  • lets the Mac's own app adapter, opened after the relay connected, read remote control from the relay and run its own private engine on the same home, where the SDK refuses the phone a chat the app holds (already has an active writer) until the app lets it go;
  • stops cleanly without writing a token or the installation ID to its log.

Every home is a fresh folder with fake ChatGPT tokens, and on macOS the run re-executes itself in a sandbox that refuses connections off this machine. The real engines put their sockets in the SDK's fixed folder /tmp/codex-daemon-<uid> and remove them when they exit; at the end the run removes any of its own that outlived their engine (new since it started, this user's, named like an SDK socket and not listening) and reports the counts as daemonSockets. It records whether an unfiltered thread/list shows the gateway chat; --expect-unfiltered-gateway-listing makes that a requirement once the router adds the legacy provider.

--shared-native-plan writes a plan that shares native chats but runs no host, so every adapter (the relay's sessions and the app's) falls back to a private engine under the native-home lease, as on a Mac whose host cannot share the app's engine. That mode passes only where private engines share the home (0.4.7 and later); on an exclusive lease the app's adapter fails to start beside the relay's session.

--test runs the relay tests and then the patched SDK's remote_control suite with its locked dependencies, in .state/native-relay-build/sdk-target. It requires 0 failures and a named list of gateway and upstream tests. The upstream tests enroll new mock machines, so only the SDK's own test build skips the existing-enrollment guard; the relay binary keeps it.

Current checks cover partial-frame cancellation, truncation, size limits, remote biometric restrictions, preservation of future response fields, single-write records, the unknown pong after queued replies, its absence on tracker-side ends, bounded stream ends under a full queue, shutdown ordering, sequence holes, and the reset switch. The shared router's live model changes, steering, permissions, and goal operations passed Claude and Codex 2 tests. Native rendered checks and daemon restart during saved chat recovery must pass before declaring this transport ready.
